scope: A declared field action determines its quadratic modes. The native finite current and complete finite scalar records are separate computed source results.
inputs: canonical Lorentz kinetic terms and field domain
units: Quadratic Standard Model formulas use hbar=c=1. The Dirac panel writes c explicitly and mu is rest energy, so inertial mass=mu/c^2.

owner.dimension: three spatial directions and one common evolution parameter
owner.free_energies: plus/minus sqrt(c^2|p|^2+w_H^2 sigma_j(Y)^2) on the charged block

panels.title: A particle is a mode seen through its records
panels.text: A source register carries currents and interactions. With a declared spatial field action, its patterns propagate. A particle label names a stable or resonant excitation distinguished by its energy, charge, transformation and detector response.
panels.boundary: A protected defect can seed or carry such an excitation. Its topology alone does not fix a particle name or mass.

panels.title: Mass is a rest frequency, not drag
panels.text: A massive mode evolves even when its momentum is zero. In a Lorentz field its rest energy μ gives E²=c²p²+μ². The Higgs background supplies some quadratic terms that create this frequency; interactions change the measurable spectral response.
panels.boundary: A massless wave has no rest gap and can carry nonzero energy. Generic repair effort becomes a particle mass only through a proved energy and spectral readout map.

panels.title: The photon follows the light cone of its field action
panels.text: For the massless electromagnetic mode in a Lorentz-invariant vacuum, E=c|p| and a wave packet travels at c. The parameter c belongs to the common spatial and temporal units of that action.
panels.boundary: Lattice wavelengths and propagation through matter can have different group velocities. A finite carrier wave equation alone does not establish the laboratory speed of light.

panels.title: Choose the program, calculate the response
panels.text: The architecture may declare its fields, couplings, state preparation and apparatus. Its record probabilities and spectrum must follow from that program. Target masses used to choose a coupling are calibration inputs.
panels.boundary: The quadratic field census is complete for the chosen Standard Model action and neutrino extension. A complete source-to-laboratory particle identification requires the same interacting observer output map.

families.title: Electron, muon and tau: three charged matter modes
families.source_operation: Encode the lepton doublet and charged singlet-conjugate currents; the chosen family register supplies three coefficients.
families.field_nature: Each mode has left and right chiral components. A Yukawa interaction with the neutral Higgs background couples those components. Diagonalizing that coupling gives three rest frequencies.
families.mass_reason: The mass term mixes chirality even at zero momentum. In the free Lorentz action, E²=c²p²+μ² and μ=v σ(Y_e)/√2; inertial mass is μ/c².
families.readout: Prepare a charged excitation, couple to a complete detector, and infer energy from its phase or inclusive spectrum. Electron thresholds and muon/tau decay resonances use different interacting observables.
families.diagram: Two chiral arrows exchange through a Higgs node, then three normal-mode tracks reach charged detector records.
families.caveat: The three family labels and numerical Yukawa matrix are program inputs unless computed from a declared source controller. Free action masses do not supply interacting measured masses.
families.status: exact quadratic consequences of a declared action; physical identification requires its observer map
families.antiparticle_meaning: The conjugate excitation carries opposite additive gauge charges and the same mass in the declared CPT-compatible relativistic action.

families.observable: renormalized mass in a stated scheme and scale; no isolated colored asymptotic particle
families.title: Quarks: matter modes that also carry color
families.source_operation: The same internal current register supplies a color-triplet weak doublet and color-antitriplet weak singlets; attach their full fermion operators and gauge links.
families.field_nature: Up-type and down-type Yukawa matrices couple the chiral color-carrying fields to the Higgs background. Their singular values give the two sets of three action masses; their left-frame mismatch gives weak mixing.
families.mass_reason: M_u=v Y_u/√2 and M_d=v Y_d/√2. The color field interacts with these modes, so a running quark mass requires a renormalization scheme and scale.
families.readout: Color-singlet hadrons, jets and decay records constrain quark properties. An isolated quark is not a laboratory asymptotic particle.
families.diagram: Three color strands enter a Higgs coupling, then feed a jet/hadron detector rather than a free-quark click.
families.caveat: Matching the internal color and weak weights supplies candidates. The interacting continuum, confinement observables and numerical Yukawa matrices require their declared realization.

families.observable: flavor production and detection; superposition of nu_1, nu_2, nu_3
families.title: Neutrinos: neutral weak-production and detection channels
families.source_operation: The neutral member of each lepton doublet has Q=0. A chosen Dirac-singlet or Majorana effective interaction supplies a neutrino mass term.
families.field_nature: The fields ν1, ν2 and ν3 propagate with their mass energies. Electron-, muon- and tau-neutrino labels describe weak production/detection combinations; different phases change the flavor probabilities.
families.mass_reason: Dirac: M_ν=v Y_ν/√2. Majorana effective theory: M_ν=v²κ/(2Λ), diagonalized by Takagi factorization. Absolute masses and the extension are separate inputs.
families.readout: A source prepares a flavor channel and a weak detector records a charged lepton after propagation. Keep all flavor, no-detection and failure outcomes.
families.diagram: A weak source splits into three mass-phase tracks that recombine at electron/muon/tau detector branches.
families.caveat: The minimal fifteen-state matter representation has no neutrino mass interaction. Assigning all three masses zero fails the oscillation target; flavor labels are not individual mass eigenstates.
families.status: exact quadratic consequences of a declared action; physical identification requires its observer map
families.antiparticle_meaning: Dirac neutrinos have distinct conjugate states. Majorana fields are self-conjugate, with distinct weak detection helicity channels.

families.observable: massless unbroken electromagnetic gauge field; two helicities
families.title: Photon: the unbroken electromagnetic wave
families.source_operation: Read loop curvature from seam potentials. Gauge shifts change local coordinates while preserving that curvature; the finite Maxwell action and evolution govern the declared field response.
families.field_nature: In the chosen electroweak phase, one mixture of the neutral weak field and hypercharge field leaves the Higgs background unchanged. This is the electromagnetic field A.
families.mass_reason: A=(g′W3+gB)/√(g²+g′²) is the exact null direction of the Higgs gauge-mass form. It has no Higgs-generated rest-energy term; a moving photon carries E=c|p| in the Lorentz vacuum regime.
families.readout: Prepare an electromagnetic field excitation and couple its energy to an absorbing detector. The detector location is a measurement outcome; a universal sharp photon position operator is not assumed.
families.diagram: Two neutral gauge arrows combine into a background-preserving direction, then a transverse wave reaches an absorber.
families.caveat: The finite carrier has its own oscillator spectrum. Identifying its detector response with laboratory photons requires a spatial continuum, state, clock and electromagnetic coupling map. Finite-lattice group velocity need not equal c.

families.observable: eight massless Lagrangian gauge fields; no isolated colored asymptotic particle
families.title: Gluons: the interacting color connection
families.source_operation: The native internal interface supplies eight independent noncommuting color currents. A declared gauge-link field transports those color coordinates between sites.
families.field_nature: The color gauge field responds to color currents and to itself because its generators do not commute. The Higgs doublet is a color singlet, so its background gives no color gauge-boson mass term.
families.mass_reason: All eight Higgs-generated color mass entries are zero. Yang-Mills self-interaction and confinement can generate a physical energy scale without inserting a gluon mass into the gauge action.
families.readout: Color-singlet hadrons and jets carry the observable evidence. A zero gluon Lagrangian mass does not imply an isolated massless colored particle in the spectrum.
families.diagram: Noncommuting color-link transports meet at a three-way interaction node and terminate in color-singlet detector products.
families.caveat: Eight current generators do not determine the strong coupling, confinement scale or complete scattering spectrum.

families.observable: massive vector resonance; three quadratic polarizations
families.title: W+ and W−: charged weak-field excitations
families.source_operation: The source weak raising and lowering currents obey [Q,T±]=±T±. A declared weak gauge field couples to those currents.
families.field_nature: The W directions rotate the neutral Higgs background into a different weak direction. The background contributes a quadratic energy cost, giving the charged vector fields a rest frequency.
families.mass_reason: W±=(W1∓iW2)/√2 and m_W²=g²v²/4 in natural units. Three scalar orbit directions supply the longitudinal components of W± and Z.
families.readout: Weak decay and scattering products reconstruct a charged vector resonance, with all competing decay and no-detection channels retained.
families.diagram: A weak-current arrow tilts the Higgs background, then a charged vector resonance branches into decay records.
families.caveat: The exact quadratic mass follows from the declared action and background. Loop corrections and resonance widths require the interacting calculation.

families.title: Z: the neutral weak-field direction that feels the background
families.source_operation: Combine the neutral weak current and hypercharge current using the declared couplings.
families.field_nature: The neutral combination orthogonal to the photon changes the Higgs background. It acquires a rest frequency while the photon direction stays massless in the quadratic action.
families.mass_reason: Z=(gW3−g′B)/√(g²+g′²), with m_Z²=(g²+g′²)v²/4. Its charge is zero and it has three massive-vector polarizations.
families.readout: Neutral-current scattering and the complete decay spectrum reconstruct the Z resonance.
families.diagram: Two neutral arrows split into a flat photon direction and a curved Z direction, with the Z branch ending in decay records.
families.caveat: The photon/Z mixing angle depends on the chosen gauge couplings; the action Hessian does not determine those couplings.

families.title: Higgs: the radial fluctuation of the symmetry-breaking field
families.source_operation: A declared complex scalar doublet couples to the source matter currents through gauge-invariant pair creation and annihilation. In the continuum completion, choose its potential and phase.
families.field_nature: The neutral background is a reference configuration. A Higgs excitation changes its radial size. The potential curves along that direction, producing a restoring frequency; its cubic and quartic terms also make it interact.
families.mass_reason: V=−λv² H†H+λ(H†H)² gives m_h²=2λv². The same background enters |D H|² and Yukawa terms, producing W/Z and fermion masses. It does not act as friction.
families.readout: A scalar excitation is inferred from its complete decay products and resonance energy distribution. Its spin-zero transformation follows from the declared scalar field action.
families.diagram: A radial pulse moves in the curved Higgs potential, with side branches showing W/Z and left-right matter couplings.
families.caveat: The 307-state finite quantum-Higgs block has its own computed transition gap and complete detector. Equating that gap to the continuum radial Higgs mass requires an explicit field/state/scaling map.

finite_Higgs_vs_continuum.finite: H in a conserved 307-state sector has two bright levels and 305 retained dark levels. Delta=sqrt(d^2+4g_pair^2), g_pair^2=4 Tr(Y^dagger Y); the gap is inferred from complete sequential records.
finite_Higgs_vs_continuum.continuum: A chosen color- and charge-preserving Higgs phase has radial Hessian 2 lambda_H v^2. This is the tree mass-squared coefficient in its canonical continuum action.
finite_Higgs_vs_continuum.distinct_symbols: g_pair is the finite pair-vertex strength; electroweak g is a gauge coupling. These are different operators and domains.
finite_Higgs_vs_continuum.required_join: An explicit embedding, state and scaling map must transport the finite complete correlators and instruments into the continuum radial field before the gaps can be equated.
